key_insight: Logarithmic qubit counts do not guarantee practical quantum modal analysis: deflation accuracy, circuit expressibility, and measurement costs remain critical.
engineering_relevance: The framework evaluates whether variational quantum eigensolvers can reliably recover structural vibration modes and support damage localization.
method: Use Cholesky whitening to align quantum-state orthogonality with structural mass orthogonality.
Derive a necessary-and-sufficient deflation penalty threshold and bound approximate-projector effects.
Separately assess mapping, ansatz expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, and finite-shot uncertainty.
evidence_signal: For 128-DOF chains, consistent-mass whitening increased Pauli terms from 576 to 2950; first-mode frequency RMS error was 2.45% at 100,000 shots per term, while an oracle-state study localized 10% stiffness loss in 84.5% of trials.
watch_item: No speedup is claimed; operator growth and measurement demand can outweigh compact qubit encoding, and oracle-state localization does not establish end-to-end performance.
paper_title: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
